v2_amended_by: DE 208, at the coordinator's instruction, on REV 162's finding
why_v2_exists: REV 162: the primary statistic's SIGN MODE was undeclared, and `asymmetry()` offers two. After the draws land, choosing between them would be a choice made on seen data -- rule 11, the rule that voided this programme's last set of results. So it is fixed BEFORE any draw completed.

item_12_sign_mode.the_deciding_reason_is_about_the_NULL_no: Under OWN_SIGN every draw partitions its OWN book by its own per-window sign, so each draw's A is computed on a DIFFERENT partition from every other draw's and from the observed. A null whose statistic is computed on a different partition per draw is not a null OF THE SAME STATISTIC, and no number of draws repairs that. Under BASELINE_SIGN the observed and all draws are scored on THE SAME windows.
item_12_sign_mode.the_second_reason: BASELINE_SIGN is the only one of the two under which a policy cannot improve its score by MOVING a window between buckets. A window the baseline scored negative that the arm nudges barely positive would, under OWN_SIGN, both add to ret_pos and remove from ret_neg -- rewarding re-labelling rather than avoidance.
item_12_sign_mode.this_reason_pre_existed: v1's own docstring states the property before any draw: 'BASELINE_SIGN -- the partition fixed by the baseline, so the arm cannot move windows between the buckets it is scored on.' v2 adopts a reason that already existed rather than inventing one.
item_12_sign_mode.if_it_had_been_arbitrary: it would have been picked by a rule stated in advance and said to be arbitrary. It is not arbitrary: the first reason above is decisive on its own.

item_13_what_must_not_be_claimed.why: REV 162: the matched control shrinks BOTH tails BY CONSTRUCTION, so it removes the FIRST-ORDER de-levering effect and not all of it. The exact-zero result holds only on an exactly-symmetric fixture.
item_13_what_must_not_be_claimed.the_true_statement: matching on cancel count, side and hour removes the first-order de-levering effect, so what A measures is the part of the tail asymmetry that a same-sized random cancellation policy does not reproduce.

item_14_matching_unit.ground_1_rule_2: CLAUDE.md rule 2: 'Rows are actions. One row per cancellable generation. If several rows can share one outcome, the evaluator must DE-DUPLICATE TO ACTIONS or the result is inflated (measured: 1.99 rows/fill, MAX 23).' The blocking measurement found up to 23 cancels on ONE reference generation (09-04 CONDVALUE) -- the same 23. This is the shape rule 2 was written for.
item_14_matching_unit.ground_2_R870: The USER already ruled that a draw resamples THE CANCELLABLE GENERATION. The unit the null RESAMPLES and the unit the control MATCHES ON must agree, or the control is matched on a different object than the test resamples.
item_14_matching_unit.what_it_replaces: the cancel-count demand, which `de_matched_cancel_control.demand_from_arm` REFUSES on this data by design -- it counts cancels while `draw_one` samples distinct generations, which is exactly the mismatch that guard exists to catch.

item_15_disclosed_cost_of_the_ruling.what: matching on DISTINCT generations UNDER-MATCHES raw exposure wherever the arm cancelled one generation repeatedly. A control given N generations may remove LESS exposure than an arm that cancelled 23 times on one of them.
item_15_disclosed_cost_of_the_ruling.direction_of_the_bias: TOWARD FINDING THE ARM SKILFUL. The control is the weaker de-leverer, so the arm's measured advantage over it is an UPPER BOUND on the part that is not exposure.
item_15_disclosed_cost_of_the_ruling.status: KNOWN, RULED AND DISCLOSED -- a cost of the ruling, not a defect found afterwards
item_15_disclosed_cost_of_the_ruling.why_a_field_and_not_prose: rule 35: a limitation that lives only in a report does not travel with the number
